Interface StaticOptimizations.SetOnce

All Known Implementing Classes:
ServiceIndex
Enclosing class:
StaticOptimizations
@Internal public static interface StaticOptimizations.SetOnce
Marks an optimization that can be set at most once: setting a second value of its class fails, instead of replacing the first one. It is for an optimization that describes the whole application, of which two values cannot both be right. Such an optimization can be read with find(String).

  • Method Details

    • find

      static @Nullable StaticOptimizations.SetOnce find(String optimizationClassName)
      Returns, if it was set, the set-once optimization of the named class.

      Unlike StaticOptimizations.get(Class), the lookup is by class name, so a caller does not have to load the class of an optimization that was never set, and the read is not recorded, so it does not make a later StaticOptimizations.set(Object) fail. That is safe for a value that is never replaced, as long as the caller calls this method on each use instead of keeping the result: a read that comes before the value is set, for example from a StaticOptimizations.Loader that runs before the loader of the value, finds nothing, and a later read finds the value.

      It neither runs the loaders nor waits for them: it returns what is set so far, which is nothing before the loaders run. Any static method of StaticOptimizations would run them on the calling thread, whose context class loader may not see them, such as a thread of the fork-join pool. Or it would wait for the thread that runs them, which may wait for the caller in turn: a loader that looks services up with fork-join tasks, when one of those services looks a service up from the thread of the pool that instantiates it. It is why this method is not a static method of StaticOptimizations.

      Parameters:
      optimizationClassName - the name of the optimization class
      Returns:
      the optimization, or null if it is not set
